cards.explanation: The answer is False. The woman answers the serpent, “We may eat the fruit of the trees of the garden…” Only the tree in the middle of the garden is the exception. She read the whole sign, friends, not just the first word. The serpent's question made it sound like a whole lot of NO, and she didn't let it stand.

The answer is that they will die. The woman tells the serpent that God has said, “You must not eat of it or touch it, or you will die.” Notice she even adds “…or touch it…” She's repeating the warning, friends, and she's not shrinking it down to something small. Then the serpent answers with, “You will not surely die…” Those two lines are going head to head.

The answer is that he tells her she will not really die. The serpent says, “You will not surely die…” She has just told him that God said they would die, and his answer is a flat contradiction. No warm-up and no hedging, just a smooth NO. Then he keeps talking, this time about what God knows (Genesis 3:5).

The answer is God. The serpent says, “…you will be like God, knowing good and evil.” Not like angels, not like kings. Like God. That's not a small offer, friends, and it comes straight from the serpent's mouth.

The answer is that she takes the fruit and eats it. The text says it plainly: “…she took the fruit and ate it.” I think this is one of the quietest, heaviest moments in the whole Bible. There's no big drum roll in the text. She takes, and she eats.
The answer is False. The text says she gave some “…to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.” He wasn't wandering off to check on the garden. He was standing right there beside her.

The answer is coverings of fig leaves. The text says “…they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves.” Sewing leaves together, friends. That's real craftwork. My mustache can pack a cookie box all day, but I wouldn't trust it with a sewing job.

The answer is True. The text says they “…hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.” First they heard His voice walking in the garden, and then they went in among the trees. I think that's a heavy kind of hiding. The text says it plainly.

The answer is that he was afraid because he was naked. The man says, “I heard Your voice in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself.” That's his own answer, in his own words. Notice he gives it straight when God calls out to him.

The answer is False. The man answers, “The woman whom You gave me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.” He talks about the woman, not the serpent. The serpent doesn't show up in his answer at all.

The answer is serpent. She answers, “The serpent deceived me…” and then adds, “…and I ate…” The LORD God asked her one short question, and she gave one short answer. She names the serpent as the one who deceived her.

The answer is that her seed will crush the serpent's head. The LORD God says to the serpent, “He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.” The head that gets crushed is the serpent's, since God is speaking to the serpent. The one doing the crushing comes from the woman's side of that line. The serpent's part in the verse is the strike to the heel.

The answer is True. The LORD God says to the woman, “Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.” It comes right after what He says about pain in childbirth. It's a heavy part of what He tells her.

The answer is through toil. The LORD God says, “through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life.” Toil. Even the word sounds tired, friends. That's what the ground will take from him from now on.

The answer is dust. The LORD God says Adam will return to the ground “…because out of it were you taken.” Then He says, “For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.” Dust is the word He uses for what Adam is. It's a heavy line, and the text just says it plainly.

The answer is that she would be the mother of all the living. The text says Adam named his wife Eve “…because she would be the mother of all the living.” The man is Adam, and his wife is Eve. It's the reason the text gives, so it's the one I'll go with.

The answer is True. The text says, “…the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and He clothed them.” Earlier they had sewn fig leaves together for themselves. Now the garments come from Him.

The answer is False, friends. The man doesn't stay in the garden. The text says the LORD God “…banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.” Right before that, the LORD God speaks of the man reaching out to take from the tree of life and living forever (Genesis 3:22). I think this is one of the heavy parts of the story.

The answer is cherubim and a whirling sword of flame, friends! The text says He “…stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life.” Cherubim AND a sword of flame that whirls. I think the way back looks closed here, and that part is heavy. But the story isn't over.

The answer is east. The text says He “…stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden…” East is where they stand, along with the whirling sword of flame. That's the side the text names, friends.
